findings.text: In the already-installed branch, EXIT_CODE is declared with `local EXIT_CODE` and never initialised. The checks are inverted (`-ne 0`) and the variable is unset when NVM_UPGRADE_NPM is not 1, so `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]` fails with an error. Default packages and reinstall-packages are therefore skipped on a plain `nvm install <installed version>`. If npm upgrade succeeds (EXIT_CODE=0), they are also skipped. They only run when the previous step failed.

The alias step uses `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]`, so `nvm install --alias=foo <installed version>` never creates the alias on success. It only runs after a failure. If EXIT_CODE is unset, the test errors and the alias is skipped. The final `return $EXIT_CODE` with an unset value also returns the status of the last command rather than a reliable result.

nvm_install_default_packages assigns EXIT_CODE without declaring it local, so it overwrites the caller's EXIT_CODE variable in nvm(). It also drops the dedicated `nvm_get_default_packages` failure early-exit that used to run before install. A malformed default-packages file is now only detected after node has been installed, not before.

The `EXIT_CODE=-1` initialisation was removed. When no install branch sets EXIT_CODE, later `[ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]` tests on an unset variable error out, or the default-package and reinstall steps are skipped or misreported.

2.reason: The non-local EXIT_CODE does no harm because every caller sets EXIT_CODE=$? right after the call, but the patch does remove the early nvm_get_default_packages check that returned before installing, so a bad default-packages file is now only caught after node is installed.

3.reason: In the already-installed branch, `local EXIT_CODE` is declared with no value and only gets set when NVM_UPGRADE_NPM=1, so otherwise `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]` becomes `[ -ne 0 ]`, which errors and skips the default-packages, reinstall and alias steps; switching the test to -eq would still fail, so this is a separate problem from the inverted test.
